strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas#66698 (GH#65733 regression in zoneinfo fallback bounds calculation) by running the newly-added tz_localize overflow test that should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime. The buggy revision returns a wrapped/NaT-based misclassification (ValueError for nonexistent or silent NaT) so the assertion expecting OutOfBoundsDatetime fails; the fixed revision raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with message matching "overflows past".

environment.python_version: 3.11 (choose one supported by your CI; exact minor not critical unless your platform constrains it)
build_commands: python -m pip install cython numpy python-dateutil pytest
pinned_because: pandas requires Cython to build from source (documented in README).

NumPy is a documented dependency; no explicit version constraint was provided in the evidence, so keep it at the version your environment uses or pick a stable widely-tested version (e.g., latest supported) to avoid unrelated failures.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit 1a559bfdfae0), the parametrized call dti.tz_localize("America/New_York", **kwargs) does NOT raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with match "overflows past" (either misclassified as a nonexistent time ValueError or returns NaT/other behavior), so the test’s with pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime, match="overflows past") fails. On the fixed revision, the same call raises OutOfBoundsDatetime whose message matches "overflows past" for all kwargs in [{}, {"nonexistent":"NaT"}, {"nonexistent":"shift_forward"}], so the test passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: Use the boundary-adjacent wall time dti = DatetimeIndex([Timestamp(Timestamp.max._value - 2 * 3600 * 10**9)]) and localize it to "America/New_York" to force the zoneinfo fallback path to derive candidate UTC instants that may wrap/underflow in int64 if bounds checks are missing.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ValueError: ... is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time (misclassification instead of OutOfBoundsDatetime)

risks: This repro relies on exercising the zoneinfo fallback path in tz_localize_to_utc / _get_utc_bounds described in the evidence. If your environment selects a different tz_localize implementation path (e.g., not using zoneinfo fallback, or using cached transitions instead), the buggy behavior may not occur and the test may pass even on the buggy revision.

Platform/toolchain constraints: the evidence mentions special casing for tzdata on Windows/Emscripten; on those platforms the availability/behavior of zoneinfo data may differ. Prefer a Linux environment with system/zoneinfo data available.

Dependency versions: no exact NumPy/pandas constraints were provided beyond documented dependency existence, so extremely old/new versions could alter tz conversion behavior enough to mask the regression. If the test doesn’t fail on the buggy commit, try matching the pandas CI dependency set (or try a couple of nearby NumPy versions).

Timezone data differences: the specific zone America/New_York and its DST transition behavior are assumed; if tzdata is missing or differs, the misclassification/nonexistent behavior may not line up. Ensure tzdata is present (or use a system image with zoneinfo).

oracle.reference_source: pandas PR#66698 test diff and PR description: regression should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with match "overflows past"; before fix it was misclassified as nonexistent time ValueError or returned NaT when nonexistent='NaT'.
oracle.why: The added test asserts OutOfBoundsDatetime and matches the substring "overflows past". The bug leaves UTC bounds as NaT due to wrapped candidates failing the round-trip check, which results in wrong control flow (ValueError for nonexistent or silent NaT) instead of the OutOfBoundsDatetime path.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The context’s before-fix behavior indicates the call will not raise OutOfBoundsDatetime("...overflows past...") for at least one kwargs value. Concretely, it may raise ValueError about a nonexistent time (for default nonexistent handling) or return NaT silently (for nonexistent='NaT'), so pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime, match="overflows past") fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After the fix (using checked_sub/bounds guards in the zoneinfo fallback candidate UTC derivation), dti.tz_localize("America/New_York", **kwargs) consistently raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with a message containing "overflows past" for kwargs in [{}, {"nonexistent":"NaT"}, {"nonexistent":"shift_forward"}].
